#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the saved project and publish readiness only after both HTTP checks pass.
set -euo pipefail
cd "${PROJECT_DIR:?}"
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?}" "${APP_URL:?}"
PORT="${APP_PORT:-3000}"
export PORT
startup_timeout="${STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-600}"
[[ "$startup_timeout" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/bin/time -p test -f start.sh
/usr/bin/time -p bash -n start.sh
current_commit="${CHECKPOINT_COMMIT:-}"
previous_commit=""
[[ ! -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit" ]] || previous_commit="$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit")"
# Reuse an in-flight build for this checkpoint when a readiness retry returns.
starting=false
if [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit" ]] && [[ "$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit")" == "$current_commit" ]] && /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null; then
  starting=true
fi
if [[ "${RESTART_APP:-false}" == true ]] || { [[ "$starting" == false ]] && { [[ -n "$current_commit" && "$previous_commit" != "$current_commit" ]] || ! /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; }; }; then
  /usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux kill-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || true
  /usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/reclaim-preview-port.mjs"
  /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
  # Pass paths through tmux's environment; keep the script in the foreground.
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux new-session -d -s app-server -c "$PROJECT_DIR" \
    -e "RUNTIME_DIR=${RUNTIME_DIR:?}" -e "OPENCODE_WEB_DIR=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" -e "PORT=$PORT" -e "STARTUP_LOG=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.log" \
    'bash start.sh > "$STARTUP_LOG" 2>&1'
fi
ready=false
for ((attempt=0; attempt<(startup_timeout + 1) / 2; attempt++)); do
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
[[ "$ready" == true ]] || { echo "Local startup failed after ${startup_timeout}s. Inspect app.log." >&2; exit 75; }
/usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
# Local readiness is independent of a temporary public tunnel failure.
/usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit"
for ((attempt=0; attempt<12; attempt++)); do
  status="$(/usr/bin/time -p curl --silent --show-error --location --max-time 10 --output "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/public-readiness.log" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$APP_URL")" || status=000
  if [[ "$status" == 2* ]]; then
    /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$APP_URL" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
    if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT:-}" ]]; then
      /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/heartbeat" >/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo 'Local and public preview are ready.'
    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ "$status" == 4* && "$status" != 408 && "$status" != 429 ]]; then
    echo "Public preview rejected the request (HTTP $status). Inspect public-readiness.log." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
echo 'Public preview did not become ready.' >&2
exit 75
---

Static HTML app on port 3000. Good. We'll build a highly polished mobile-first Turkish text game.

Let's plan the design thoroughly.

## Game concept

Title: "Gece Devriyesi: Seul'ün Siyah Taytı" or something. Korean female cop in Seoul, night patrol. Text-based interactive fiction, Turkish. The protagonist is a Korean police officer. Sensitive emotional threshold, all four choices in each segment, events chain, choices branch, endless.

Need to make an actual playable game with:
- Splash/home screen with title, protagonist, start/continue, wardrobe access.
- Phone-fit layout (100dvh, max-width 480px, safe-area).
- Header: night clock / day / stats.
- Main "scene view": location, atmospheric illustration (CSS gradient + SVG scene), narrative text, 4 choice buttons each with icons, tags/consequences.
- Stats: Duygusal (emotional composure), Ayak Konforu (foot comfort), Temizlik (shoe cleanliness), Şüphe/Reputation, Arrest count, Cry counter? Sand/water in shoes tracking, scent level.
- Inventory/wardrobe: 32+ socks, 32+ shoes (flats/babet and heels), each with stats (comfort, cushion, sand protection, water sensitivity, scent). Choose socks and shoes daily. Main character wears black super tight painful tights (tayt) + skin-colored brief socks(?) — "ten rengi külotlu çorap" actually likely "ten rengi külotlu çorap" = skin-colored pantyhose? User wrote "deti rengi külotşu çoraplı" -> "ten rengi külotlu çoraplı" likely skin-tone pantyhose. And "babetli" flats. But later wants 30+ socks and high heels. So: base outfit is black very tight tights (tayt), plus skin-tone pantyhose layered? Hmm "siyah çok sıkan acıtan taytlı ve ten rengi külotlu çoraplı ve babetli". So black tight tights, skin-colored pantyhose socks, and flats. Then high heels wardrobe. Could be: daily outfit choose a sock (çorap) from 34 and shoe from 34 (heels and flats). The "signature" default is black tights + skin tone pantyhose + black flats. We can model layering: tights always worn (black, painful), and select "çorap" (which is actually pantyhose/socks) and shoes. But requirement says each day choose socks and shoes. Let's show "Siyah sıkı tayt: her zaman üstünde (acıtıyor)". And then socks (34) and shoes (36). Good.

- Story engine: Need lots of content and endless. Use a graph of nodes with 4 choices each. Each choice leads to another scene. No ending. Long enough. We can create maybe 40-60 hand-written nodes across city duty, beach/port, driving chase, night market, etc., with event triggers. Plus procedural "patrol generator" that creates endless chains from event templates with 4 choices, stateful variables. Better: hand-written 25-30 hub event nodes + procedural endless chain filler with templated events that feel authored. Ensure event-event triggering. Every choice leads to a distinct event id. Need "4 choices in every section" — every node exactly 4 choices.

- Event chain: choice can set flags, stats, schedule next node. Some events trigger follow-ups via flags: e.g., water in shoe => next event "Islak Çorap" with options (dry, change, ignore...). The engine uses `next` from each choice, plus "trigger" queue. We can implement event triggers: each choice may add pending events; when choosing next, pending event overrides unless choice has explicit next? Requirement event-event triggers. Better: every choice has `next` (distinct path), and additionally may `trigger` a follow-up event that gets queued and appears after 1-2 scenes. We can show "Zincir: ..." indicator. Implement `after` chain: choice.next can be an event, and event may have `onEnter` effects. If choice adds `queue`, the queued event is inserted after the immediate next scene. Guarantee event-event trigger visible.

- No ending: Endless. We can display "Sonsuz devriye — bitiş yok". Every scene's choices all exist. Death? User says no ending. Avoid death. Even if stats zero, she cries etc. but loops. Stats can bottom/top. Use "emotional limit narrow" mechanic: when composure low, choice text changes? We can add "gözyaşı" meter. If composure < 20, "ağlama" overlay tears and auto-cry event but not end. We could include a "Ağlama krizi" event queued.

- Night patrol always. Each day cycle: "Gün X • 23:00" to 05:00. Each "vardiya" ends at dawn -> "Gün bitti" report screen -> wardrobe for next night -> continue. Infinite days. The user wants every day choose socks/shoes, always night patrol. So implement shift: each scene advances clock 8-20 min, from 21:00 to 05:00; at dawn show "Vardiya Raporu" with stats and then wardrobe screen to pick next night's socks/shoes; next day starts. Since no endings, day continues forever.

Potential issue: choices per scene and content breadth over many days. Procedural template pool of maybe 30 events with 4 choices each and variants, plus handcrafted arcs. We can write rich content in JS data. Quality matters. Number of nodes: target ~36 core nodes (each 4 choices = 144 distinct branches) plus procedural. That's a lot of writing but doable. Need Turkish text quality, with correct Turkish characters. User's typing is broken but we should write proper Turkish.

Content design:

Character: "Yuna Park" (Korean female cop, 27), Seoul Metropolitan Police, night patrol. Partner "Min-ho" maybe. Car "Gece 07". Setting: Seoul, Han River, Itaewon, Myeongdong, Gangnam, Dongdaemun, Mapo, Namsan, Bukchon. Since Turkish text but Korean setting. The user said Korean female cop. Night patrol.

Tone: atmospheric, emotionally fragile, sensory details about tight tights, socks, shoes, water/sand. Slightly melancholic, intimate, with a dash of wry humor. The game should handle foot care as central mechanic. Avoid sexualization; focus on sensory/emotional. The "külotlu çorap" is a garment; keep tasteful.

Stats:
- `sinir` (duygusal dayanıklılık 0-100) starts 34 ("çok dar")
- `konfor` (ayak konforu 0-100) starts 62
- `temizlik` (ayakkabı temizliği 0-100) starts 88
- `nem` (ıslaklık) 0-100
- `kum` (kum) 0-100
- `koku` 0-100
- `itibar` 0-100 (mesleki itibar)
- `tutuklama` count
- `gözyaşı` count
- `şüphe` heat? maybe.
- `enerji` 0-100.
- `çorap`, `ayakkabı` selected.

## Objective
- Türkçe, telefona uygun, oynanabilir ve sonu olmayan metin tabanlı bir gece devriyesi polis oyunu oluşturmak.
- Mevcut depodaki uygulamayı tamamlayıp çalıştırma ve test yöntemleriyle doğrulamak.

## Requirements
- Koreli kadın polis Park Yuna; gece sahil devriyesi ve zaman zaman şehir görevleri.
- Duygusal hassasiyet, dikkatsizlik, ayakkabıya kum/su kaçması ve temizlenmezse deniz kokusu gibi durumlar.
- Şehirde araç kullanırken kaza olasılığı.
- Her bölümde dört seçim; farklı dallar ve olayların birbirini tetiklemesi.
- Günlük çorap ve ayakkabı seçimi; 30’dan fazla çorap ve topuklu ayakkabı seçeneği.
- Devriyeler daima gece yapılmalı; oyun çok uzun ve sonu olmamalı.
- Tamamlanmış, oynanabilir oyun oluştur; açıklama isteme, varsayımları kısaca bildir.

## Decisions
- Oyunun adı “Gece Devriyesi”; başkarakter Park Yuna, Seul Gece 4 biriminde.
- Vardiya 21:00–05:00; şafakta rapor gösterilip yeni gece başlıyor, oyun bitmiyor.
- Her gece gardırop seçimi ve iki hazırlık hakkı; durumlar, kayıt ve dallanan olaylar tasarlanıyor.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` içinde ana ekran, gardırop, hikâye, rapor ve yardım/durum panellerinin iskeleti oluşturuldu.
- `data/wardrobe.js` içinde 36 çorap ve 36 ayakkabı seçeneği eklendi; 26 ayakkabı topuklu.

- Projenin çalıştırılması ve tarayıcıda mobil görünüm/oynanış testleri yapılmalı; son JPEG ekran görüntüsü alınıp incelenmeli.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. `game.js` dosyasındaki `// __PART2__` noktasından devam edip hikâye akışını, seçimleri, olay zincirlerini, gece sonu raporunu ve tüm düğme/klavye etkileşimlerini tamamla.
